code:
# Step 1: a factorial that receives "itself" as its first argument
# If we call it "self", the recursive call becomes self(self)(n-1)
step1 = lambda self: lambda n: 1 if n == 0 else n * self(self)(n - 1)

# To call it, we must pass it to itself:
factorial_v1 = step1(step1)

print(factorial_v1(5))   # 120
print(factorial_v1(7))   # 5040
description: Implement factorial without a recursive name by passing a copy of the outer function to itself.

steps.description: Define step1 to accept a function self first and return an inner lambda taking n.
In the recursive branch, self(self) passes self to itself to get the inner function of n, then applies that function to n - 1.

steps.answer: It returns the inner lambda (lambda n: 1 if n == 0 else n * self(self)(n - 1)) with self bound to step1.
steps.question: What does step1(step1) return when assigned to factorial_v1?

steps.description: Bind factorial_v1 = step1(step1) and call it on 5 and 7 to compute 120 and 5040.
Step into factorial_v1(5) to see each recursive call pass self to itself before decrementing n.

title: Recursion by Self-Application
